questions.stem: What are the new coordinates of point (3, 4) after a counterclockwise rotation of 90 degrees around the origin?
questions.solution: When a point is rotated counterclockwise by 90 degrees around the origin, its x-coordinate becomes the negative of the y-coordinate and its y-coordinate becomes the x-coordinate. So (3, 4) becomes (-4, 3).
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of rotating points about the origin.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget that the x-ordinate becomes the negative of the y-ordinate and vice versa.

questions.stem: What are the new coordinates of point (5, -2) after a clockwise rotation of 180 degrees around the origin?
questions.solution: A rotation of 180 degrees around the origin flips the point across the origin, so (x, y) becomes (-x, -y). Thus, (5, -2) becomes (-5, 2).
questions.explanation: This question assesses knowledge of rotating points by a full turn.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Students might accidentally apply a counterclockwise rotation instead of clockwise, leading to the incorrect answer A.

questions.stem: What are the new coordinates of point (-1, 3) after a rotation of 270 degrees counterclockwise around the origin?
questions.solution: A rotation of 270 degrees counterclockwise around the origin is equivalent to a clockwise rotation of 90 degrees. The x-coordinate becomes the negative of the y-coordinate and the y-coordinate remains unchanged. So (-1, 3) becomes (3, -1).
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of rotating points by different angles.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Students might confuse the clockwise and counterclockwise rotations, leading to an incorrect choice.
